💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that the Illinois Clean Ports Program is putting $104 million behind efforts to help clean up its working waterfronts, funds earmarked for heavy-duty electric equipment assets that includes forklifts, giant reach stackers, switcher locomotives, and the charging equipment needed to support them.
  • Procurement is now underway for zero-emission vehicles, equipment, and supporting infrastructure at four sites across the state.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that the Illinois Clean Ports Program is putting $104 million behind efforts to help clean up its working waterfronts, funds earmarked for heavy-duty electric equipment assets that includes forklifts, giant reach stackers, switcher locomotives, and the charging equipment needed to support them. There’s even a passenger ferry!

Procurement is now underway for zero-emission vehicles, equipment, and supporting infrastructure at four sites across the state. Administered by the Illinois Environmental Protection Agency (Illinois EPA), Illinois’ Clean Ports Program aims to modernize operations at ports and waterfront facilities in Chicago, the Quad Cities, and southern Illinois’ river port districts.

Recent findings suggest that “Illinois’ waterways are a competitive advantage for the state,” noted Illinois Governor JB Pritzker, who was elected to a historic third term on 03NOV. “By modernizing port infrastructure, advancing zero-emission technology, and improving air quality, we are strengthening our economy while building a cleaner future for Illinois.”.

Illinois’ Clean Ports Program isn’t just replacing diesel-powered equipment with electric alternatives – instead, the initiative also includes Level 2 and DC fast charging, shore power and charging for electrified ships, and comprehensive grid upgrades designed to modernize existing port operations and support the deployment of newly introduced electric equipment.

Recent findings suggest that the program takes a holistic approach to port electrification at Chicago’s Illinois International Port District (IIPD), treating energy generation, storage, and deployment as parts of a single connected system. On-site solar helps meet the port’s growing electricity needs while excess power is stored for peak hours, when grid electricity is most expensive. This setup reduces strain on the local grid, and acts as a hedge against rising energy costs.

Recent findings suggest that for smaller public port districts, replacing aging equipment and upgrading electrical infrastructure can be an enormous financial undertaking. The Illinois Clean Ports Program helps make those investments possible, bringing cleaner, healthier, zero-emission technology within reach of terminal operators while preparing the state’s ports for a more competitive freight future.

Slay the Spire 2: 10 Best Fool Cards, Ranked

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1675 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dualshockers

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that finally, the Slay the Spire 2 community has been blessed with a newly introduced character, and this one packs some serious firepower!
  • Sources indicate that but just who is this mysterious Fool, and what powers do they wield?
  • Of course, you also have your bow and arrow cards that can deal serious burst damage, the Stretch mechanic, which is great for blocking, and the Sadness mechanic, which can help you prolong your turns.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that finally, the Slay the Spire 2 community has been blessed with a newly introduced character, and this one packs some serious firepower! The Fool is the newest addition to the Spire, and they’ve got their sights set on bringing down the Architect once and for all.

Sources indicate that but just who is this mysterious Fool, and what powers do they wield? Well, there are quite a few powerful gimmicks in this deck, the most broken of which are the Wah Cho Ki cards. These are melodies, kind of like the Defect orbs that, when played, help you trigger other powerful cards.

Of course, you also have your bow and arrow cards that can deal serious burst damage, the Stretch mechanic, which is great for blocking, and the Sadness mechanic, which can help you prolong your turns.

It has been revealed that but which of these cards are the most powerful for a deck, and which ones should you always be on the lookout for? Let’s dive right in!

Encore is a fun one, massively helping you extend your turns and get the most out of a tricky hand all for the great cost of 0 energy!

Once played, you gain one energy and draw two cards. However, you can only play one more card for the rest of the turn. Realistically, you should play this when you've exhausted your energy and want to eke out a little extra block or damage.

However, there are a couple more ways to play this. You can use it for a substantial card, or extend your energy for an X-cost card like Repeat Shot. Furthermore, if you manage to clone this card, Encore actually stacks on top of itself, replacing the effect every time you play it. Playing multiple copies of this leads to some ridiculous turns.

I put these two cards together because they serve a pretty similar purpose, and well, it’s probably not worth having both in your deck unless it’s specifically set up for that.

According to recent reports, both of these cards do a huge amount of single-target damage using your arrow. Sky Shot is easier to get, as it’s just a rare card, and it has Innate, giving you a ridiculously strong first turn and often ending fights before they even begin.

Divine Shot, on the other hand, is an upgrade of Foolish Shot and can be found by picking the Archaic Tooth Relic from Orobas. This also does a huge amount of damage, costs 0 energy, and even has Retain, so you can use it on the turn it's most effective. While these cards pack a punch, it is always worth being cautious about how many Bow cards you have in your deck. If you don’t have a spare arrow, it’s basically a curse!

Recent findings suggest that sadness, for the most part, is generally a pretty bad thing in STS 2. It clogs up your hand and is a bit of an eyesore. But that doesn’t mean it’s useless. If you can turn this Sadness into Joy with a card like Punch of Joy or Ecstasy, it can become a blessing.

Now, on a card like Brighten Up, we have an engine with an upside and a downside, but if you have the required pieces, Brighten Up can be doubly beneficial!

When played, this card gives you 2 Sadness and 2 Joy, or 3 Joy when upgraded. For one energy, you’re basically getting three more energy and three free draws, making it an incredible card for extending your turns and ending fights without taking damage. If you have a way to get rid of that Sadness, then this card is unreal.

Recent findings suggest that motif, at first glance, might seem a little weak to some. two energy is a lot to spend on a card that doesn’t do anything immediately. However, upgrading this halves its cost, making it way more playable.

In a recent development, motif draws you an extra card every time you gain a melody, so that you can draw up to three extra cards per turn. The thing is, when you have a small deck and not much energy generation, this often doesn’t help much.

Which, of course, means that Motif should be a card picked up in the latter half of your run, when you have more resources available. When you start getting longer turns, and your deck has more powerful individual cards, Motif suddenly becomes extremely potent.

The thing is, a lot of cards in Slay the Spire only become good at a certain point in time, or when paired with something else to allow a certain combo. You know what’s better than that? Something that’s cracked right out of the box!

Cho Firm is one of those cards, and one that’s pretty easy to overlook. So long as you have an arrow available, which is most of the time if you’re playing a melodic-based build, you’ll gain double the block from this card. Generally, this’ll give you 12 block for one energy; however, there are plenty of ways to enchant this, and whatever you gain from the first block will double.

According to recent reports, and of course, if this wasn’t powerful enough, you’ll also gain a Cho melody, activating cards like Song Path, Motif and Wah Blast. For a common card, this one is a must-pick for every deck.

I mentioned Wah Blast in the previous entry for good reason. This card is an absolute monster! For starters, playing this card normally deals 14 (18) damage to all enemies. That’s already decent.

However, it gets even better when you pair this with other melody cards. If you have a Cho or Ki melody, playing something like Cho Firm will make this attack hit twice! That’s 28 (36) damage across the board with a single attack and very little set-up.

And of course, like Cho Firm before it, this activates any card that wants more Wah melodies, like Violent Chord, Motif or Rhythm Strike. Under the right conditions, paired with Violent Chord, this card can wipe out entire multi-enemy combats in a single turn. No more losing Max HP from those pesky biting books in Act 3!

If you happen to come across Darv in Act 2 or 3 and see the Dusty Tome on offer, well, drop everything, because things are about to get absurd!

Picking up the Dusty Tome gives you the Lost Lute, a Power card that plays the top card from your deck every time you gain a Melody. Do I have to explain how ridiculous that effect is? Getting multiple melodies in a single turn is pretty easy, and this Power can even play you more melodies, meaning more cards!

It has been revealed that at three energy, this is a pretty expensive card, but unlike the other Form cards, upgrading it reduces its cost to two, making it much easier to slot in. While it might be tough to get this card to work in the 2nd act, it really shines in Act 3, and if you manage to cheat it out with something like Jewelled Mask, you can win entire runs with this card alone.

And speaking of broken three-cost cards, we have Mythic Form, which honestly might be the most powerful Form card, beating out Echo Form and Void Form for the title.

In a recent development, at the start of your turn, you’ll get a random Tarot card added to your hand. But just what are these Tarot cards, and what do they do? Well, Tarot cards are stupidly broken: they all have 0 energy and can do anything from giving you seven energy to instantly killing anything under 30 HP, dealing damage based on what floor you’re on, and giving you an extra turn, among others!

Sources indicate that similar to Lost Lute, the only tough thing about this card is finding time to play it. As soon as you start gaining the effects from this card, you just begin to steamroll! But for a form card, this feels pretty fitting! Let’s just hope it doesn’t get nerfed too hard!

If you enjoyed using Wah Blast, meet its older, more powerful brother, Wah Symphony!

According to recent reports, wah Symphony deals six damage to all enemies… sounds pretty bad, right? Well, this card gains an extra four (six) damage for every other card containing Wah Cho or Ki in your deck. Now, suddenly, simply by owning other good cards that you’re going to be using all the time, this card skyrockets in power.

According to recent reports, it’s pretty normal for this card to deal 40+ damage to every enemy every time you use it, and of course, if you have something like Bag of Marbles, it can often end fights on Turn 1. And as usual, I have to mention it also procs cards that benefit from Wah, making it even more powerful. This card is wildly strong!

Let me introduce you to the ultimate card in the Fool’s portfolio. Yep, with a name like Wah Cho Ki, I’m sure you can already imagine why this card is pretty broken… but I’ll break it down.

In a recent development, for starters, for one energy, this card deals 9 damage, gives you 9 block and draws a card. Upgraded, this goes to 12 damage and two cards! Already, these are ridiculous numbers for a single energy, giving you a bit of everything!

Of course the real potential of this card comes from the synergies it allows. And those synergies are… well, all of them! Yep, this single card gives you every melody, so any other card that requires even one is immediately fulfilled. So if you have Song Path, Violent Chord and Motif, this card basically doubles in power.

It sounds simple on paper, but when you think about how much this card actually does, you’ll be terrified when Mega Crit comes in with the nerf hammer!

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, physical buttons have a lot going for them.
  • According to recent reports, as CarMoses first discovered, Audi has filed for a patent application that describes a motorized switch bar, which pivots out from behind the display’s lower edge.
  • Sources indicate that for those who do want the physical buttons, there are plenty of reasons to get excited.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, physical buttons have a lot going for them. They’re easy to find by feel, satisfying to use, and generally pretty good at staying wherever the automaker installed them. Well, it seems Audi has an idea that would change that last part: it involves hiding the buttons behind a touchscreen, then deploying them when needed.

According to recent reports, as CarMoses first discovered, Audi has filed for a patent application that describes a motorized switch bar, which pivots out from behind the display’s lower edge. The screen stays fixed, while the physical controls swing into position beneath it. Interestingly, when stowed, the bar apparently has an on-screen counterpart with the same functions lined up in the same order, so those who don't want physical buttons can avoid them entirely.

Sources indicate that for those who do want the physical buttons, there are plenty of reasons to get excited. First, Audi indicates in its patent documents with the German government that the switches can deploy at startup, via voice controls, or via gestures. Moving the controls from the screen to the physical switches also provides more total screen room for customers. (In one example, the physical bar deploys when a movie opens, leaving more room for the video.).

Ultimately, this could be a great way to meet the demands of more people. Designers love a clean dashboard without physical buttons and switches. Plenty of drivers really love having that switchgear. This system allows owners to pick whatever they want on the fly.

Industry observers note that the timing makes plenty of sense too. Audi has openly noted that it views moving toward more mechanical controls as the right direction. Of course, adding extra complexity to the once-simple idea of buttons also can increase the cost down the line when it comes time for repairs, but even so, this idea is certainly a fascinating solution to a very modern problem.

BYD's Latest SUV Can Hide Its Steering Wheel When You Don't Need It

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that I have to admit that when I first saw the Fangchengbao Tai 9 stow its steering wheel away on social media, I assumed that it was AI. It wasn't. This BYD brand's fresh SUV can indeed retract its steering wheel right into the dashboard. However, it’s not quite used for the reason you’d think.

Sources indicate that the Tai 9 is a six-seat, plug-in hybrid SUV about the same size as the Cadillac Escalade IQ, and it sits at the top of the Fangchengbao range. BYD’s Chinese-market brand and naming structure can be confusing, but in essence, Fangchengbao is one of BYD's premium brands.

It has been revealed that power comes from two electric motors that produce 536 horsepower at peak, while a 1.5-liter turbocharged engine is responsible for any combustion-powered driving. The Tai 9 has a 66.5 kWh battery that is capable of BYD’s flash charging technology. The brand claims it can sprint from 10% to 97% in nine minutes.

Industry observers note that those are all very compelling specs, but the most interesting part of the Tai 9 is the top-of-the-line Foldable Smart Cabin trim. Since the Tai 9 uses a steer-by-wire system, the steering wheel can fold up and stow itself in the dashboard. BYD claims that takes about 10 seconds.

According to recent reports, however, this isn’t for any sort of autonomous driving. China’s autonomous driving rules are strict, and no automaker in the country has approval for commercially sold eyes-off, hands-off driver assist features. Instead, the folding steering wheel is primarily for comfort and space, specifically when the car is stationary. Photos of the feature in action show that stowing away the steering wheel makes extra room for a little table setup.

According to recent reports, this isn’t entirely unprecedented. The new trend in China is for large SUVs to be third spaces where buyers can comfortably hang out, even when they aren't driving. The Tai 9’s Nappa leather, comfy seats, and second-row folding screen are meant to make it a calming, relaxing space to spend time. It's similar in concept to what we’ve seen on the Zeekr Mix and SkyNomad N90 Studio.

Still, despite the Tai 9’s folding steering wheel not being for self-driving, I wouldn’t be surprised if it does show up in cars for that reason someday, as manufacturers strive to make cars that can truly drive themselves.

A car with no steering wheel at all might feel risky and uncomfortable to some car buyers, especially if it's like Tesla’s Cybercab, which can’t be driven manually at all above low speeds. Yet, if there were a backup to take control, I could see that putting some minds at ease.

Recent findings suggest that the Fangchengbao Tai 9 is on sale in China for about $42,000. The top-of-the-line model with the foldable steering wheel is about $49,500.

Recent findings suggest that well, here’s something to melt your face right off: the secret prototype M7 BMW never made. Powered by the 4.9-liter V-8 that would go on to make the E39 M5 such a legend, it's a manual-transmission 1997 short-wheelbase E38 7-series, a total wolf in sheep’s clothing.

Instead, the V-12-powered 750iL that Pierce Brosnan pilots remotely from the back seat in 1997's Tomorrow Never Dies provided plenty of drama.

BMW financed a series of films in the early 2000s featuring Clive Owen as a nameless driver, collected together as The Hire, and the one Guy Ritchie directed featured Owen ferrying Madonna around at breakneck speed in an M5. Sadly, like the E31-chassis, V-12-powered M8 prototype, the M7 would never make its way to a production version. Scientists discover a hidden eye disease that slowly steals night vision

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1049 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, A newly identified genetic eye disease can gradually interfere with night vision and the ability to see objects at the edges of the visual field.
  • An international research team, including scientists at the Scheie Eye Institute within the University of Pennsylvania's Perelman School of Medicine, traced the condition to a gene already associated with another form of vision loss.
  • Although the condition has not yet received an official name, researchers are calling it EFEMP1-associated late-onset retinal degeneration (L-ORD).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, A newly identified genetic eye disease can gradually interfere with night vision and the ability to see objects at the edges of the visual field. The condition may be especially difficult to recognize because people can maintain good eyesight for much of their lives before noticeable problems develop.

An international research team, including scientists at the Scheie Eye Institute within the University of Pennsylvania's Perelman School of Medicine, traced the condition to a gene already associated with another form of vision loss. However, the two diseases affect eyesight in strikingly different ways. The previously known disorder primarily damages central vision, while the newly discovered condition affects peripheral vision and the ability to see in darkness.

Although the condition has not yet received an official name, researchers are calling it EFEMP1-associated late-onset retinal degeneration (L-ORD). It is linked to a specific genetic variant known as p.Arg140Trp in the EFEMP1 gene. This change causes an unusually thick accumulation of material between cells in the eye.

A Genetic Discovery That Began Decades Ago.

Recent findings suggest that the investigation traces back to 1998, when doctors documented an unusual pattern of vision loss in a family in the United States. As researchers uncovered new genetic evidence, they were able to connect those findings to families in Europe who revealed similar symptoms.

The study, published in JAMA Ophthalmology, examined three unrelated families from different countries who carried the p.Arg140Trp variant. Their symptoms were compared with those of another family carrying a different change in the same gene, called p.Arg345Trp, which is associated with the previously recognized disease affecting central vision.

The international collaboration included researchers from Penn Medicine, the University of Edinburgh, the University of Basel, Charles University, and the University of Bonn.

It has been revealed that at first, scientists suspected that the unusual symptoms in the original family might be caused by a different genetic disorder. Testing, however, failed to identify the variants responsible for that condition.

Sources indicate that "The different disease expression in this family was thought to be similar to a condition caused by C1QTNF5 gene variants. However, none of the variants associated with that disease were found," remarked Artur V. Cideciyan, PhD, an ophthalmology researcher and co-director of the Center for Hereditary Retinal Degenerations. "Our collaborators then discovered a new variant in the EFEMP1 gene that normally causes a different disease where the macula, which is tied to central vision, is affected first.".

How the New Eye Disease Affects Night Vision.

In a recent development, the researchers found that the newly identified condition develops gradually in the outer regions of the retina. Located at the back of the eye, the retina detects incoming light and transforms it into signals that the brain uses to create visual images.

Unlike the previously known EFEMP1 disorder, which initially affects the macula and central vision, this newly identified disease begins in the peripheral retina. People may see normally for much of their lives before gradually noticing that their side vision is narrowing or that seeing in dim surroundings has become more difficult.

Problems may be particularly noticeable around dusk or at night, when the eyes must rely more heavily on specialized light-sensitive cells called rods.

One reason the disease is challenging to diagnose is that these cells may initially show no visible structural damage. The gradual progression of symptoms can make the condition even harder to recognize.

However, the researchers identified a potentially valuable early clue. In affected individuals, rod cells take unusually long to recover when the eyes move from bright surroundings into darkness. This abnormal response can be detected even when the retina still appears structurally normal.

Recent findings suggest that "We can detect a major abnormality in the way rod photoreceptors recover in darkness with retinas that still look structurally intact," Cideciyan stated. "This gives us a functional marker of disease at a stage when photoreceptor cells have not yet been lost.".

The finding suggests that changes in how the retina functions may reveal the disease before the light-sensitive cells responsible for vision begin to disappear.

What the Discovery Could Mean for Age-Related Vision Loss.

An important question remains unanswered: How many people carry this newly identified genetic variant?

It has been revealed that researchers suspect the condition is relatively uncommon, but they do not yet have enough information to determine its prevalence. Larger investigations will be necessary to establish how frequently the variant occurs and how many people may be affected.

Sources indicate that beyond identifying another inherited eye disorder, the findings could help scientists better understand why vision deteriorates with age. Studying rare genetic diseases can reveal biological processes that may also contribute to much more widespread retinal conditions.

Recent findings suggest that "Aging is a risk factor for many medical conditions, including retinal diseases such as age-related macular degeneration, the most common retinal condition of aging," remarked Tomas S. Aleman, MD, a professor of ophthalmology and the other co-director of the Center for Hereditary Retinal Degenerations. "Lessons learned from these infrequent, late-onset genetic eye diseases offer glimpses at possible mechanisms of disease for much more frequent retinal problems.".

Recent findings suggest that by revealing how different changes in a single gene can produce distinct patterns of vision loss, the research adds to scientists' understanding of inherited retinal disease. It also highlights the potential importance of detecting changes in visual function before damage becomes apparent in the retina's structure.

The study received support from the University of Edinburgh Chancellor's Fellowship award, RS Macdonald Charitable Trust Seedcorn Award, the BrightFocus Foundation (M2024009N), the German Research Foundation (532367710), the Medical Research Council (MC_UU_00035/9, MC_UU_00007/10), the Swiss National Science Foundation (204285), the Ministry of Health of the Czech Republic (NW24-06-00083), Charles University in Prague (UNCE/24/MED/022 and SVV 2600631), and the Samuel G. Jacobson, MD, PhD, Memorial Fund.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • The Belgian developer is returning to the series it created with Divinity, a non-numbered sequel that’s designed for new and veteran players alike.
  • According to recent reports, larian calls Divinity its most ambitious title ever, with the studio striving for a level of depth and breadth we’ve not seen before.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that larian Studios has delivered what was arguably the biggest reveal of The Game Awards 2025 showcase. The Hellstone, the mysterious monolith in the desert that’s been generating a lot of speculation in the lead-up to the show was indeed teasing the studio’s next game.

The Belgian developer is returning to the series it created with Divinity, a non-numbered sequel that’s designed for new and veteran players alike. The announcement was entirely cinematic, setting the tone for what looks to be the next substantial thing in the space.

According to recent reports, larian calls Divinity its most ambitious title ever, with the studio striving for a level of depth and breadth we’ve not seen before. This is the next project from the Baldur’s Gate 3 team, after all, so there’s understandably immense anticipation for it.

Divinity is a standalone RPG, and does not require you to have played Divinity: Original Sin, or Divinity: Original Sin 2. If you did, however, you’re going to find the journey extra special because of the continuity it offers.

“We’re ready to bring everything we’ve done previously into one place,” noted founder and game director, Swen Vincke.

Sources indicate that “This marks the beginning of something with more breadth, depth, and intimacy than anything we’ve created before. We’ve been building toward this moment ever since we took our fate into our own hands. This is the Divinity we’ve always wanted to make and you're going to have loads of fun with it.”.

Recent findings suggest that beyond that, there’s precious little that’s been revealed for Divinity so far. We don’t know what platforms it’s going to be coming to, nor do we even have a release target. We do know it’s an RPG, so you can very much expect something similar to earlier games in the series, and, of course, Baldur’s Gate 3.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, for decades, Briggs & Stratton has helped keep the lights on after the storm with its gas-powered generators. Now, the firm is bringing that legacy to the electric age with a latest 16 kWh backup battery designed to scale with your growing energy needs.

Briggs & Stratton partnered with Texas-based EG4 to offer an all American-branded solution for battery backup power solution last year, and its stackable SimpliPHI batteries helped make it easy to right-size home battery projects – but those batteries were limited in size, and limited in what they could actually offer. With the launch of the brand’s new, 16 kWh SimpliPHI battery, the manufacturer is ready to meet your energy needs … even if those needs take you up to 512 kWh. (!).

For context, the average US home uses about 865 kWh of energy per month, so a 512 kWh battery should theoretically keep your lights on for nearly 18 days after a storm – or provide basic power for your whole block for a weekend, at least!

It has been revealed that “This launch represents a significant shift in our battery strategy,” explains Sequoya Cross, vice president of energy storage at Briggs & Stratton. “Our combined resources allow us to bring a competitively priced battery of the highest quality to energy storage installers.”.

An onboard battery management system (BMS) and built-in Wi-Fi gateway help to streamline the system’s setup for installers, while the Briggs battery’s automatic inverter sensing technology supports closed-loop communication with Sol-Ark, Solis, EG4, Growatt, Megarevo, Victron, and other leading inverters. Other installer-friendly features include an IP65-rated enclosure allows for indoor or outdoor installation in either ground- or wall-mounted setups without requiring an additional cabinet, and an integrated circuit breaker that allows technicians to isolate the battery during servicing.

According to recent reports, the battery itself is rated for 8,000 cycles at 90% depth of discharge, with a charge and discharge rate of 0.5C and an end-of-life capacity of 70%. Briggs & Stratton backs its newly introduced battery packs with a 12-year parts warranty that includes labor and travel costs, as well as a US-based tech support service.

The SimpliPHI 16 is available for pre-order now, though pricing was not mentioned in the original press release.

SOURCE: Briggs & Stratton Energy Solutions.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Chinese automakers are trying to capture as much of the European car market as possible, and they’re resorting to clever marketing tricks that legacy automakers have used in the past to attract buyers.
  • BYD is one of the many Chinese car companies trying to rack up orders, and its Denza brand has now recreated a famous Volkswagen commercial from two decades ago that involved a diesel-powered SUV and a jumbo jet.
  • In a recent development, I vividly remember when I saw the original clip 20 years ago.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Chinese automakers are trying to capture as much of the European car market as possible, and they’re resorting to clever marketing tricks that legacy automakers have used in the past to attract buyers.

BYD is one of the many Chinese car companies trying to rack up orders, and its Denza brand has now recreated a famous Volkswagen commercial from two decades ago that involved a diesel-powered SUV and a jumbo jet. Only this time, Denza has an ace up its sleeve, and it’s quite impressive.

In a recent development, I vividly remember when I saw the original clip 20 years ago. A blue Volkswagen Touareg V10 diesel towed a 171-ton jet aircraft down the same Dunsfold runway in the United Kingdom where the old "Top Gear" episodes used to be filmed.

In a recent development, now, the Denza B5 (or Bao 5 in some markets) plug-in hybrid SUV is back at the same place to do the same stunt, but adapted for a 2026 where everything seemingly needs to be bigger, more over the top, and more in-your-face. (I blame TikTok.).

So, we have a Chinese PHEV that uses two electric motors and a 1.5-liter gas engine. It’s all-wheel-drive, its 31.8-kilowatt-hour battery can deliver up to 56 miles of all-electric range on a full battery, and it has two mechanical locking differentials. This last part is important. The battery can be fast-charged at up to 100 kW, and the total system output is a healthy 536 horsepower, with most of that oomph being provided by the two e-motors.

We also have a 207-ton jumbo jet that got a quick repositioning for no other purpose than pure entertainment.

Here comes the interesting bit: While Volkswagen’s original stunt kept all four of the Touareg’s wheels in place—you know, how a car usually works—BYD decided to put its PHEV SUV to the test by gradually removing some wheels.

Recent findings suggest that the first run was done with all four wheels in place, followed by a three-wheeled run with 2.2 tons of ballast. For the final act, both right wheels were removed, and the ballast reached 5 tonnes. During the three runs, the Denza B5 towed the Boeing 747-400 over one mile, and best of all, it used exclusively electric power.

In a recent development, the point of it all? Promote the newly introduced SUV to the UK market, where the Land Rover Defender is among its biggest rivals. Unlike the Defender, however, which is now based on a unibody design and is primarily combustion-powered, the Denza B5 sits on a bespoke ladder-frame chassis and more substantially electrified. It has a gas engine that acts mainly as a generator for the high-voltage battery. The battery cells are directly integrated between the chassis rails.

According to recent reports, if you're thinking about trying this stunt at home, just know the vehicle needed a few modifications to pull it off. BYD added a custom towing attachment, removed some seats to make room for the ballast, and added stabilizers to make up for the missing wheels.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Enhancement: This article was originally posted on May 14, but we wanted to update it with news of the election result.
  • According to recent reports, christian Mango is ten years old, and was encouraged by his elementary school class to write a letter about a topic of his choice, and mail it to a decisionmaker.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

An 83 year old Congressional representative who sent an embarrassing letter to a well-meaning 10 year old constituent on the topic of electric cars and climate change, where she seems to brag about saddling his generation with debt through a recent climate rollback she voted for, has lost her seat.

Enhancement: This article was originally posted on May 14, but we wanted to update it with news of the election result. After a recount, Chuck Hubbard has defeated Virginia Foxx by 330 votes, and will go on to represent NC-5 in Congress.

According to recent reports, christian Mango is ten years old, and was encouraged by his elementary school class to write a letter about a topic of his choice, and mail it to a decisionmaker. Christian chose his Congressional representative, 83 year old Virginia Foxx.

Foxx is an 11-term Congresswoman in North Carolina, one of the most gerrymandered states in the nation, and was expected to win a 12th term in the heavily republican district, having previously proudly touted an endorsement from an enemy of the US who tried to overthrow the government. Her opponent is Democrat Chuck Hubbard, a former journalist and native of the district.

Recent findings suggest that for the topic of his letter, Christian chose electric cars – which is what makes this story relevant to us here at Electrek. Christian laid out several points about EVs, stating that “they’re better than normal cars. They’re better for the environment. They pay less. And there’s no gas.” (All true! well done Christian).

Christian suggested that electric cars could be incentivized with a $5,000 tax rebate – lower than the $7.5k EVs used to get, but better than the $0 they get federally today (compare to the ~$20k in ignored costs that gas cars still benefit from).

Christian went on to suggest action on climate change, stating “maybe there is still a chance for 6.5 million people to not die anymore and for the weather to get better just maybe glaciers stop melting.” Christian was probably referring to the number of people who die from air pollution globally each year (though several estimates suggest that number is actually higher, and Christian did conflate climate and weather… but we’ll give him a pass on this one, his heart is in the right place).

Industry observers note that christian was proud of his letter, as was his mother, Emily Mango, who stated “he researched, cited facts, and made good arguments in his essay – an essay that had nothing to do with politics. He was proud of his essay.”.

It has been revealed that but then he got a response, and that’s when things took a turn for the worse. Christian’s mother Emily angrily shared the response on Instagram, where it gained traction.

Emily mentioned Foxx’s screed was “disrespectful, hostile and unkind” and called it “demoralizing and reprehensible.” She said she had to speak to her son and teach him that this response was “not okay,” and that “nobody should talk to a child like that and nobody should talk to a teacher like that.”.

I’d also add that it’s full of disinformation, and that it even seems to brag about the massive debt that Foxx has imposed on Christian’s generation.

Industry observers note that foxx includes six links, all from propaganda publications that deny the science of climate change. 3 are from from WSJ (2 of which are opinion pieces) and 1 is from Fox, both of which are owned by the same climate denier, Rupert Murdoch. 1 is from Washington Times, a tabloid founded by a religious cult (yes, really), and 1 is from another right-wing climate denying publication, National Review.

Notably, none of the six links have anything to do with electric cars.

In the text of the response, Foxx touts republicans’ “all of the above” energy policy, which is ironic given that the party whose energy policy she touts has spent most of the last year forcing broken dirty coal plants open (which they are still doing after ruled illegal) and trying to shut down clean cheap ones. Apparently “all of the above” is code for “fossil fuels and nothing else.”.

Recent findings suggest that foxx’s letter does not directly address the strengths of electric cars, despite them being the subject of Christian’s letter. Notably, EVs actually can receive energy from any generation method, whether it be wind, solar, or even coal or gas – whereas gas-powered vehicles can only use one type of energy, oil. Thus, an “all of the above” strategy should probably find EVs the preferable route for transportation.

But in apparent contradiction to Foxx’s surely sincerely held belief that we should pursue an “all of the above” energy policy – which electric cars would help to achieve – she in fact has voted against EVs when given the opportunity.

Foxx claims in her response that she can’t support tax credits on electric cars, because those go to “mostly people with higher incomes who are able to purchase ‘newly introduced’ electric cars.”.

But she in fact voted against, and later voted to repeal, incentives which were limited to lower-income-earners and were only available on cars up to a certain MSRP cap. Further, they were available on used vehicles, not just upcoming ones – suggesting that Foxx doesn’t know what she voted against.

Foxx was one of 218 republicans to vote in favor of a ~$4 trillion giveaway to wealthy elites. Her vote raised electric bills and threatened US energy security and surrendered US manufacturing jobs to China. Some of the money given away to wealthy elites in the bill was clawed back from energy efficiency programs that had been going to regular Americans.

According to recent reports, those energy efficiency programs had been instituted by the Inflation Reduction Act, the Biden-era law which established tax credits for EVs and other efficiency rebates. The Inflation Reduction Act was actually revenue positive, which is to say it reduced the national debt (by $238B), rather than adding to it, because of provisions to increase enforcement against wealthy tax cheats.

But most of the IRA was repealed by the bill that Foxx voted for, meaning the US lost out on those deficit reductions. All in all, the bill Foxx voted for would add $4 trillion to the national debt – which, incidentally, is another point Foxx touches on in her response.

In one sentence, she seems to directly mock Christian, telling him that “YOU and your classmates will be responsible for that debt” as part of a warning about the dangers of government debt.

Industry observers note that but I read this sentence as mockery, rather than as a sincere warning, given that Foxx voted to add $4 trillion to the national debt, which she, at 83 years old, knows she will not have to pay off. Christian, who is 10, will likely spend his whole life saddled with the debt Foxx voted for.

Recent findings suggest that he will also have to pay for her inaction on climate change, which will have increasingly worse effects on the world Christian will grow up into. Foxx’s generation has already felt the heat, with the massive floods that devastated her state in 2024, from a hurricane that was made 200x more likely due to climate change. Now, imagine how much worse it could get if Foxx’s policies remained in place until 72 years from now when Christian will be her age.

Foxx then closes out the letter with disparaging remarks about teachers, claiming that they are “too interested in indoctrinating you,” and warning Christian about “propaganda.” Which I guess shows where Foxx’s attitude comes from – if she has spent her 83 years never trusting anyone who knows more than her about a topic, that would certainly lead to the ignorance reflected in her letter.

Foxx – who somehow has a doctorate in education and presently sits on the Congressional education committee – could have turned this into a nice moment to teach the child who wrote her something about democracy and responsive government, but instead turned it into a moment to teach the world what’s wrong with her.

When we first wrote this article in May, Foxx had a projected 97% chance of winning in a district which voted for her by a 19% margin in 2024.

But that was before America (and its short memory) was reminded of how incapable republicans are of leading anything.

After a pile of economic crises caused by Donald Trump’s incompetent “leadership,” and his continued participation in an 8-month-and-counting war of choice that is spiking energy prices worldwide, bringing oil profits to record highs (and attempting to distract the news from talking about the Epstein files, which he is heavily featured in and has tried to cover up), America was once again fed up. And his incompetence took his entire party down with him.

Safe republican seats were flipped around the country in the biggest “wave” election we’ve seen in recent times, with the Democrats gaining control of both the House and Senate.

And it looks like Democrat Chuck Hubbard, a Wilkes county native and former journalist, who also ran against Foxx in 2024, will now get his chance to represent the people of North Carolina’s 5th district, after winning by 330 votes in a recount.

The situation in North Carolina is particularly interesting, given that republicans had done an emergency redraw of district lines in an attempt to cheat their way to winning more seats.

It has been revealed that generally, district lines get redrawn after each Census, which happens on the decade mark, rather than mid-decade. But republicans saw ahead of time that they were likely to lose the House due to their unpopularity, and wanted to fudge the numbers in several states instead of going for a fair fight.

So they engaged in Gerrymandering, a process wherein district lines are redrawn to favor a particular political party. The idea is to put as many of your opponents’ votes into a few safe seats as possible, while spreading out your own votes to a wider range of seats that you win each by a small margin.

Industry observers note that foxx’s main argument against Christian’s suggested $5,000 EV incentive, is increasing national debt. Yet in just one tax bill, her approval increases the national debt over 10%. This is not Christian’s “responsibility”, this burden is forced on him, along with climate change.

Recent findings suggest that but it turns out that republicans were even more unpopular than they thought, and as a result, their Gerrymandering backfired. Those narrow margins they sought ended up flipping more seats than would have otherwise flipped, turning North Carolina almost completely blue in what analysts have called a “Dummymander“. (NC-5 itself was not one of the redrawn districts, though – it just swung 19 whole points to the Dems).

After a nail-bitingly close election, Foxx requested a recount. The margin is extremely thin, just 0.12% of votes, but today Foxx called to concede, making it the last decided House race of the election, giving Democrats a 258-seat majority.

It has been revealed that foxx previously vowed to run again in 2028, hoping for a less hostile political environment. She will be 85 years old at the time of that election.

This EV-Swapped 1967 Porsche 912 Has 300 HP And A Split Battery Pack

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, inverted is a name that's been around for a while in the EV-swap world.
  • In a recent development, according to Piston Heads, the owner of this specific 912 had already swapped a more potent 911 engine into its rear end, but wanted something even better suited for daily driving.
  • Recent findings suggest that there's some clever engineering here, too.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, inverted is a name that's been around for a while in the EV-swap world. It started out doing electric powertrain swaps for classic Range Rovers, which it still does. But it also has a bespoke program now, under which it will develop custom EV swaps for customers for any sort of car they want. In this specific case, Inverted stuffed some batteries and an electric motor into an old Porsche 912. Interestingly, this is the third powertrain that's been in this Porsche.

In a recent development, according to Piston Heads, the owner of this specific 912 had already swapped a more potent 911 engine into its rear end, but wanted something even better suited for daily driving. So they took their car to Inverted and the team got to work. The end result is a car that looks exactly like a normal Porsche 912, with all of its gorgeous old-school styling, but drives like a modern EV.

Recent findings suggest that there's some clever engineering here, too. The 62 kWh battery pack is more than enough to propel the vintage Porsche's featherweight body a fair ways. However, that's a lot of weight to hang over the rear axle. Air-cooled Porsches were already prone to lift-off oversteer, so they don't need any more. So Inverted came up with an interesting solution: split the pack into two parts. On section is mounted out back where the engine used to be, and the other is under the hood. It means the electric 912's weight balance is actually better than the original car's.

Recent findings suggest that inverted claims that this EV 912 has around 250 miles of range, and it can DC fast charge at 75 kW. The latter might seem weak in the world of modern EVs, but it's perfectly fine in a classic like this. This is a daily driver, not a long-distance cruiser. So 250 miles is more than enough for daily usage, and plugging it in overnight to charge will get the owner a fresh battery in the morning.

The rear-mounted electric motor makes 300 horsepower, so it's much more potent than the original 912 four-cylinder engine which made around 90 horsepower. Inverted indicates it can hit 0-60 mph in four seconds, which kicks the ass of the stock vehicle. The original 912 took about 13 seconds.

In a recent development, this isn't just a powertrain swap, either. Its interior is completely redone and it's gorgeous. The gauges look like vintage Porsche gauges but they're modified for EV used. For example, the classic Porsche central tachometer was replaced with a power percentage gauge. The fuel gauge is now an analog battery charge gauge, too. It's just lovely.

This is an awesome project and one that would make for an incredible daily driver. It has modern Porsche levels of performance, with modern EV levels of range, in a stylish vintage package. Seems perfect.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that A Mercedes-Benz executive coupe from the early 1990s is a grand tourer par excellence, and you could hardly do better than this well-traveled machine. Presently on Bring a Trailerr (which, like Car and Driver, is part of Hearst Autos), this is a European-spec 1991 560SEC that was imported first to Japan before being brought to the United States seven years ago. The mileage is reasonable at the equivalent of 78K miles, but if you like to travel, here's your beast.

In a recent development, this generation of Mercedes coupe was the two-door sibling to the wunderbar W126 S-class, designed by the legendary Bruno Sacco. The first of these C126 coupes launched in 1981, kicking off a decade-long run that ended with the 1991 model year. These are truly great cars from the brand’s “The best or nothing” era.

See all results for used cars for sale near 29405.

U.S.-market 560s came with a fairly emissions-strangled version of Mercedes's 5.5-liter V-8, but this car benefits from higher compression and slightly freer-flowing exhaust. There were more powerful versions available, but here you can expect around 275 horsepower and mountains of creamy torque, fed through a four-speed automatic gearbox.

It's not an AMG under the hood, nor are the stately looks here anywhere near as boisterous as the wide-body versions of the 560SEC that Affalterbach dreamed up. Here, the tailoring is more discreet, set off by a set of 17-inch Lorinser wheels and a slightly lower ride height on H&R springs with Bilstein dampers up front.

It looks understated and reserved in a way Mercedes doesn't really do anymore. Inside, it's just as cushy as you would hope, with leather heated seats, plenty of wood trim, and a stereo that has been updated with Bluetooth connectivity.

There’s an matter with the air conditioning that a specialist could probably address, but this example has had plenty of mechanical work done. The fuel system was overhauled with upcoming injectors and a new distributor a few years ago, and larger work including valve seals and a new timing chain was done two years ago. At that time, perishables like vacuum lines were also replaced.

Basically, this well-fettled big coupe is an idealized version of the top-dog Mercedes from the brand’s glory days.

The auction ends on November 24.

A common blood pressure drug has a surprising effect on calorie-burning brown fat

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1188 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that A widely used blood pressure medication may have an unexpected benefit beyond its ability to control hypertension.
  • In a recent development, losartan belongs to a class of medications called angiotensin receptor blockers (ARB), which have an established safety profile.
  • Recent findings suggest that the findings also revealed a surprising connection between brown fat and mental health.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that A widely used blood pressure medication may have an unexpected benefit beyond its ability to control hypertension. Scientists have found that losartan can activate brown fat, a specialized type of body fat that burns energy, and improve metabolic activity in mice. The discovery suggests that an existing medication could potentially be repurposed to stimulate brown fat and support metabolic health.

In a recent development, losartan belongs to a class of medications called angiotensin receptor blockers (ARB), which have an established safety profile. In a fresh study published in Nature, researchers found that the drug increased brown fat activity through a biological mechanism separate from its blood pressure effects. This raises the possibility of developing treatments that activate brown fat without lowering blood pressure.

Recent findings suggest that the findings also revealed a surprising connection between brown fat and mental health. After examining data from more than 100,000 patients, researchers discovered that people with detectable brown fat had lower rates of several medical conditions, including anxiety and depression. This is the first time the research team has reported associations between brown fat and psychiatric health, adding to earlier evidence linking the tissue to better cardiovascular and metabolic health.

The research was led by Paul Cohen at Rockefeller University's Laboratory of Molecular Metabolism, working with Heiko Schöder and Daniel Lafontaine from Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center (MSKCC). It expands on research published in 2021, when Cohen's team analyzed approximately 50,000 patients and found that those with more brown fat had substantially lower odds of developing cardiometabolic conditions such as coronary artery disease and type II diabetes.

"We only looked for a few diagnostic codes in that study, mainly focusing on cardiovascular disease since that's what this tissue has historically been associated with," indicates Cohen. "The scope of this latest analysis is far more expansive. We doubled our number of patients and considered more than 500 codes, which allowed us to unearth many new insights.".

AI Analysis Reveals New Benefits of Brown Fat.

Recent findings suggest that to investigate brown fat's relationship with human health, the researchers examined PET/CT scans from more than 100,000 patients who had undergone imaging as part of their cancer monitoring. They focused on scans showing brown adipose tissue, which can be found in six regions of the body, including the neck, armpits, and areas around organs such as the heart and kidneys.

The team used an approach known as reverse translation, which begins with observations in patients and then investigates the biological processes responsible for them. Cohen's laboratory has previously used this strategy to uncover important details about brown fat and its effects on health.

Nicolás Gómez-Banoy, the study's first author and an endocrinologist and instructor in clinical investigation in Cohen's laboratory, used a machine learning system developed by researchers at MSKCC to measure brown fat activity. The technology allowed him to assess both the total activity in each patient and the activity within each of the six anatomical regions.

It has been revealed that the analysis showed that brown fat's location could be just as important as its presence. Activity in particular regions appeared to have stronger associations with certain health conditions, suggesting that brown fat may influence the body differently depending on where it is found.

"For example, the axillary, or armpit, area was linked to a decreased risk of high blood pressure compared to other regions," he says. "But overall, patients with brown fat have better glycemic parameters, lipid profiles, and echocardiographic indices, as well as lower inflammatory markers.".

These findings indicate that people with brown fat tend to have healthier blood sugar levels, blood fat profiles, measures of heart function, and indicators of inflammation.

Common Blood Pressure Drug Activates Brown Fat.

In a recent development, as the researchers investigated medications associated with brown fat activity, they noticed an intriguing pattern. Patients taking angiotensin receptor blockers were more likely to have detectable brown fat on their scans, suggesting that these widely prescribed medications might influence the tissue.

To explore that possibility, the team conducted laboratory experiments using cultured brown fat cells. They found that losartan directly increased the cells' metabolic activity, providing evidence that the drug could stimulate brown fat rather than simply being associated with its presence.

Even more interestingly, the researchers discovered that losartan activated brown fat through molecular pathways different from those responsible for lowering blood pressure. That distinction could be especially valuable for developing future medications that target metabolism without interfering with normal blood pressure regulation.

Industry observers note that "The fact that its different effects are mediated by different molecular pathways is advantageous, since it means we could potentially isolate them in future therapies," indicates Gómez-Banoy. "That way you would be able to stimulate brown fat in people with normal blood pressure.".

Additional experiments in healthy mice strengthened the findings. Animals given losartan showed increased energy expenditure, consumed more oxygen, and produced more carbon dioxide, all signs of heightened metabolic activity. Despite these changes, their body weight remained stable.

Brown Fat's Surprising Connection to Mental Health.

Beyond its metabolic effects, brown fat may have a previously unrecognized relationship with psychological well-being. The patient analysis revealed that individuals with detectable brown fat had lower rates of anxiety and depression, extending the tissue's potential health associations beyond the cardiovascular system.

"We know that metabolically healthy people tend to have lower incidence of psychiatric diseases, so it could be that having brown fat makes you more metabolically healthy, and this correlates with fewer psychiatric complications," claims Gómez-Banoy.

In a recent development, the researchers also found an intriguing relationship involving selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors, or SSRIs, medications commonly prescribed to treat depression. These drugs appeared to suppress brown fat activity, suggesting another possible connection between psychiatric treatments and metabolic regulation.

However, the findings do not suggest that brown fat is beneficial in every respect. The analysis also identified higher rates of osteoporosis and certain skin diseases among people with brown fat, raising questions about possible trade-offs that require further investigation.

Industry observers note that the discoveries have opened several avenues for future research. Scientists hope to examine the genetics of people with particularly high brown fat activity, investigate why the tissue is associated with lower rates of anxiety and depression, and determine whether its apparent benefits can be harnessed safely.

In a recent development, losartan may also be only one of several existing medications worth investigating. The extensive patient analysis identified additional drugs associated with brown fat activity, offering researchers a range of potential candidates for future studies.

"There were plenty of other medications associated with brown fat activity in our large cohort," Cohen notes. "This is just a start.".

Sources indicate that arc Raiders is kicking off its last major event of the year. We’ve known about the existence of Cold Snap for a while, of course, but we finally have a solid idea about what to expect.

Cold Snap is made up of different components - including fresh content - that all players have access to.

As the name suggests, of course, Cold Snap introduces the latest snowfall Map Condition. As part of this, maps will be covered in snow, thanks to snowstorms sweeping across them. For one, snowfall makes it harder to see enemies, but it also turns all lakes solid.

Staying outdoors for too long will cause you to catch frostbite, which slowly drains HP. Embark notes you’re going to need to bring more healing items with you on raids, and it doesn’t look like there are firepits that could keep you warm - though staying indoors for a while will help.

Cold Snap arrives alongside limited-time events that will be available until Tuesday, January 13. The snowfall visual patch and newly introduced frostbite mechanics are available on Dam Battlegrounds, Buried City, Spaceport, and The Blue Gate.

According to recent reports, one of the newly introduced events is Flickering Flames, which comes with its own progression track of 25 levels. Content is, of course, unlocked using Merits, which are earned from XP in matches. The other event is the Candleberry Banquet Project, which requires you to donate items found on the surface (including Candleberries).

Industry observers note that you’ll earn rewards each time, and each stage completed will reveal a new scene on the banquet table. Likewise, there are cosmetic rewards as part of each stage, and you can use it as a source of Merits, too.

Industry observers note that while on the subject, the fresh upgrade also kicks off a new Raider Deck (battle pass). Available from December 26, The Goalie Raider Deck is pretty much what you’d expect. You’ll find several pages of cosmetic and useful items. The new Deck will be available to all players for free.

Latest Update: GTA 6 Drew More Than Half of Active PS5 and XBOX Players on Launch Day

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (660 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dualshockers

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A lot of people cleared their schedules for GTA 6, and apparently they meant it.
  • Sources indicate that as Eurogamer reported, Circana analyst Mat Piscatella shared the figures shortly after GTA 6 debuted on November 19.
  • According to Piscatella's post on Bluesky, 61% of PS5 players active in the United States on November 19 played GTA 6.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A lot of people cleared their schedules for GTA 6, and apparently they meant it. New figures show that more than half of the active PlayStation 5 and XBOX players tracked by Circana played Rockstar's game on launch day. The average time spent with it was over eight hours on both platforms.

Sources indicate that as Eurogamer reported, Circana analyst Mat Piscatella shared the figures shortly after GTA 6 debuted on November 19. The numbers come from Circana's Player Engagement Tracker, which measures what people are playing rather than how many copies a game has sold.

According to Piscatella's post on Bluesky, 61% of PS5 players active in the United States on November 19 played GTA 6. On XBOX, the figure was 56% of active players worldwide. That's a huge share of the audience for one game, particularly when people still had all their usual favorites to choose from.

There's an notable distinction in those percentages. The PlayStation figure covers the US, while the XBOX figure is global, so they aren't directly comparable. They also refer to people who were active on their consoles that day, not everyone who owns a PS5 or XBOX. It would be wrong to say that more than half of all console owners bought GTA 6.

The time figures are just as wild. US PS5 players who debuted GTA 6 averaged 513 minutes with the game running, or eight hours and 33 minutes. On XBOX, the average was 494 minutes, or eight hours and 14 minutes. That measures time with the game active, rather than proving everyone was at the controller for every minute.

Sources indicate that eight hours is a full working day, and that was the average time GTA 6 was running for the players Circana tracked. You'd expect plenty of long sessions for a release this big, but those averages are still difficult to get your head around.

Eight hours is a full working day, and that was the average time GTA 6 was running for the players Circana tracked.

For comparison, Fortnite was the next closest game on November 19, with an engagement rate of about 10% among active players across the tracked console audiences. Even a game that people routinely return to every day wasn't coming close to GTA 6 on Thursday.

Piscatella also looked at what GTA 6 players had been playing in the two weeks before launch. The top five were Fortnite, Call of Duty, GTA 5, Roblox, and NBA 2K27. It's quite a mix, and it states something about GTA's staying power that the previous game was still on that list 13 years after release.

Piscatella said he couldn't remember another day like it in Circana's tracker, although its daily history only goes back to May 2020. That doesn't establish an all-time record, but it's still a striking result for the period Circana can measure.

It has been revealed that the attention around GTA 6 has been hard to miss even outside gaming circles. Lately, I've heard people who know next to nothing about video games bring it up in conversation. That's not something I can say about most fresh releases, even the ones everyone in the gaming community is excited about.

Rockstar also revealed that GTA 6 sold 32.5 million copies before release and generated an estimated $3.79 billion in day-one retail sales, including preorders. As DualShockers previously reported, that made for a record-breaking start before a PC version was even available.

Sales figures alone don't show whether people actually sat down and played. Circana's data fills in that part. A huge share of active console players had GTA 6 running on November 19, and the PC version isn't even out yet.

Industry observers note that it'll be interesting to see what happens to those figures once the initial excitement dies down. As far as November 19 goes, though, the numbers leave little doubt about where console players were spending their time.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that with declining sales, annual capacity cuts approaching a million units, and a wave of affordable Chinese competitors entering Western markets, Volkswagen is facing down its own mortality. Rather than fighting it, the manufacturer is leaning in and announcing aims to export roughly 300,000 Made-in-China VWs per year by 2030.

Sources indicate that american dealers won’t be getting any Made-in-China vehicles (not at first, anyway), but for Mexican, South American, Middle Eastern, African, and Southeast Asian markets, the shift to lower-cost Chinese manufacturing marks a major strategic pivot. In addition to exporting budget-friendly sedans like the Jetta VA3, Volkswagen is also considering a move to adopt Xpeng’s tech stack for up to 75% of its core European lineup.

Sources indicate that the move comes as Volkswagen’s Chinese JVs face a sharp sales decline in their home market, selling just 1.2 million latest cars in the first nine months of 2026 (down 35% compared to last year). The financial story is even worse, with last year’s roughly $815 million profit falling to a more than $120 million loss.

“The sharp decline in the overall market in China remains an industry-wide challenge,” said Martin Sander, Volkswagen Group’s sales boss, before adding that VW’s “new, locally developed electric models are beginning to make an impact.”.

Add in rising energy costs, continuing software complications, and serious labor disputes with the IG Metall union in Europe, and Volkswagen may not have much choice in the matter – which is why it’s not exactly surprising to see VW consider turning China into an export hub. And that 300,000 number? That may be just the start.

On Volkswagen’s third-quarter results call, CFO Arno Antlitz reportedly called that 300,000 annual export target “conservative,” adding that overseas shipments could help offset the carmaker’s weakening prospects in China.

According to recent reports, if it's good enough for Apple, then absolutely. Just put "Designed in Germany" instead of "Designed in California" on the back.

Hopefully, though they'll work towards "re-shoring" once they've got through this crisis. Certainly the European governments should support EU based firms importing EU-designed vehicles, so long as there is a plan to supply demand domestically. They should also encourage Chinese firms to build in the EU. Why transport vehicles such a long distance.

Here’s hoping those export plans eventually expand to the US. After years of pushing upmarket, seeing a reborn electric Jetta on US lots would feel like a true return to Volkswagen’s affordable and accessible “people’s car” roots.

#178174. Industry News: Waymo Is Recalling Its Robotaxis Because They're Not Great At Dealing With Human Instructions

Industry News: Waymo Is Recalling Its Robotaxis Because They're Not Great At Dealing With Human Instructions

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (954 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Insideevs

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Waymo recalled its robotaxis again on Friday, citing challenges with navigating closed freeway lanes and handling manually controlled intersections.
  • The manufacturer's robotaxis were banned from California freeways earlier this month after a few high-profile incidents.
  • The robotaxis seem to be very adept at dealing with normal road conditions.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Waymo recalled its robotaxis again on Friday, citing challenges with navigating closed freeway lanes and handling manually controlled intersections. For anyone who has been following Waymo closely, this shouldn't be that surprising.

The manufacturer's robotaxis were banned from California freeways earlier this month after a few high-profile incidents. Waymo took the voluntary step of suspending interstate operation nationwide on Wednesday, meaning the entire fleet is now back to running primarily on local roads and minor state highways.

The robotaxis seem to be very adept at dealing with normal road conditions. But the trouble seems to be when something unexpected pops up. Regulators from California cited poor behavior surrounding closed lanes and construction zones, a recurring issue for the firm, along with a another recent high-profile incident involving a California Highway Patrol rolling road block.

If you don't know what that last sentence means, you aren't alone. When I first moved to California a few years ago, I had no idea what a rolling road block or "traffic break" meant in normal parlance. But drive California freeways long enough and you'll experience one. A CHP cruiser or a group of them joins the highway, puts on its lights, and slowly zigzags across all lanes of traffic, blocking drivers from passing or exceeding the speed of the maneuver. The goal is typically to create a safe break in traffic for authorities to removed debris, clear and accident, or otherwise operate on the road. Sometimes it just slows down the herd before it barrels into a blind-corner accident scene at 80 mph.

When I first experienced this, I was plenty confused. But when I saw cops swerving in front of me with lights on, I naturally just slowed down and stayed behind me. Common sense told me that a cop swerving around with their lights on probably isn't looking for a race. Unfortunately, though, autonomous driving software doesn't always know how to interpret novel situations. So when a Waymo got caught behind a rolling road block, here's what it did:.

Industry observers note that yep, it tried to blow right by. CHP was able to hold it back, but I've seen a Trooper controlling six lanes of traffic with one car before. Add in an inventive and disobedient robotaxi and you can see how it could create a dangerous situation wherein an autonomous vehicle is driving down a road that construction workers or police think is effectively closed.

It has been revealed that now, Waymos are good enough at avoiding hitting things that I don't expect this would have been too bad. But even a small chance of a runaway robotaxi is unacceptable to regulators and to Waymo, so it's good to pause freeway operations until they figure things out.

Recent findings suggest that but the road block situation is indicative of a larger problem with autonomous vehicles, and perhaps the most interesting one. We think of driving as a predominantly legal or process-driven endeavor. You stop at stop signs, obey the speed limit, and keep it between the lines. Errors happen, but we tend to see them as based on improperly applied rules.

Yet the police here are disrupting the rules and enforcing an unscheduled and ad-hoc temporary speed limit and traffic flow. If you're from out of state or haven't experienced it yet, it's confusing, as there's direct ruleset for an impromptu situation like that. Yet any other driver caught in this situation wouldn't blow past the cop car. Like me, they'd approach it cautiously, and let the police car take the lead.

That is the problem I'm referring to: Driving is not just about rules and infrastructure. It's a social behavior. We wave each other ahead at stop signs and intersections. We signal our intent for an aggressive merge by riding the side of the lane market. You look at people's faces to gaze intention and attention. And when the traffic lights are down or the road is blocked by falling trees, we create impromptu order where chaos exists, nodding or waving to signal that it's someone else's term.

This was always going to be the hard part for robotaxis. That's why the same recall applies to another troubled behavioral pattern for Waymos: They struggle when officers or city workers are manually controlling and intersection. Whether it's due to a high-traffic event or an outage, it's not all that uncommon to see a police officer directing traffic by hand. They wave you through or hold you back.

According to recent reports, but what happens if the car loses sight of the person directing traffic? What if the person directing traffic isn't actually a police officer, and waves you through a red light? What if the alternate route the police point you to spits the robotaxi onto a highway, where it isn't allowed to go?

Sources indicate that there are a million more what-ifs related to this social component of driving. All of them will have to be encountered and solved as they come, just as you and I eventually figured these things out. Recall by recall, we'll turn these Waymos into upstanding citizens.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Tesla’s latest version of Full Self-Driving lets you swing a virtual camera around your car like you’re cruising through Leonida in Grand Theft Auto.
  • The feature is called Tesla Reality View, and it’s reaching early-access users with FSD V15.
  • According to recent reports, the manufacturer notes this new FSD version is 25 times safer when it does critical interventions.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Tesla’s latest version of Full Self-Driving lets you swing a virtual camera around your car like you’re cruising through Leonida in Grand Theft Auto. It’s a neat trick, especially when you consider that the Tesla has to generate the scenery as it goes. It also gets a little floating arrow, which now lets you know which roundabout exit it’s going to take.

The feature is called Tesla Reality View, and it’s reaching early-access users with FSD V15. The earlier parking display drew outlines of nearby objects, but this one recreates the street around you in real time and highlights where FSD intends to turn or park. You can have this on the whole screen, split it with the map, or let the map take over instead. There’s also a quieter cabin mode, and even the turn signal sound fades after a few clicks.

According to recent reports, the manufacturer notes this new FSD version is 25 times safer when it does critical interventions. The upgrade to the software that interprets camera images was trained on millions of internet videos and shared with its Robotaxi and Optimus programs. What’s not clear is the starting figure. How many miles did the previous version go between critical interventions, and under what conditions? Tesla doesn’t say.

Sources indicate that will drivers actually notice? Tesla states V15 is better at spotting potholes, small animals, signs, and debris, including chains (which have been known to cause crashes and have drawn federal scrutiny). It should also avoid deep standing water and choose more appropriate speeds in school zones and bad weather.

In a recent development, tesla states the navigation now learns from the routes other Teslas actually take, initially at the start and end of a trip. Tesla intends to extend that approach to the whole route later. Once you arrive, the map can show several parking options, and FSD uses your parking history to help pick one. It’s another application of the fleet learning feature Tesla demonstrated with V12.

It has been revealed that V15 can also slow for a speed camera, but if you override it twice for the same camera, the car will remember your preference. Bike Rack Mode lets FSD operate with a rack on the tow hitch, though it won’t automatically reverse for you at the destination, leaving parking up to you. Autopark, Summon and backup warnings are disabled in that mode.

Sources indicate that in a roughly 25-minute drive, Sawyer Merritt found V15 more cautious around pedestrians than V14. In one parking lot, he said the car braked for someone running across its path before he spotted them himself.

While parking, Merritt could see which space FSD had picked, but tapping another space did nothing. He had to switch to manual, select the spot, and reengage FSD. It then parked where he wanted. That parking maneuver makes a pretty good case for the GTA graphics, which now give you a much better idea of what’s around the car and what it’s about to do, but the 25-fold safety improvement claim will need more than a drive to Best Buy to judge.
